summary: The culprit is reachable — E2, E6 and E7 do converge on Cassandra Vole and every person the solution reasons about is in the cast — but the surrounding scaffolding contradicts itself repeatedly: the locked-door premise is broken by Priya's own discovery of the body, the blinds are drawn before the solution says Cassandra drew them, and the murder weapon (Derek's tablets) is never shown reaching Cassandra's hands while it is explicitly shown reaching Marcus's. It plays, but a careful player will hit several dead ends where the text disagrees with itself.

findings.claim: No player prompt was stored, so delivery against what was asked for cannot be judged; only the bare setting seed survives.
findings.citation: "setting_input": "Silicon Valley startup, 2001 dot-com crash, open-plan office building"

findings.claim: There is no solution.chain and no supports/exonerates/implicates fields on any evidence item; the deduction had to be audited from the prose of how_to_deduce and the single "relevance" tag per clue.
findings.citation: Step 1 — Establish access: The server closet was found locked with the master key undisturbed on its hook, yet Derek was inside.

findings.claim: Step 1's whole inference collapses because two other people got into the supposedly sealed closet — Derek himself entered it, and Priya opened it at 11:30 PM — so an unaccounted-for means of access demonstrably exists and the duplicate key is not the only explanation.
findings.citation: Only Cassandra's duplicate key (E2) explains how the closet was accessed and re-locked after the murder, immediately focusing suspicion on her despite her claimed conference-room alibi.

findings.claim: The solution has Cassandra draw the blinds after returning from the closet (post-11:05 PM), but her own alibi fixes the blinds as drawn from 10:40 PM, eight minutes before she even entered the closet — so the residue-transfer sequence in Step 3 cannot have happened in the order stated.
findings.citation: She then drew the conference room blinds and positioned herself there as a visible alibi, unaware the blind pull retained traces of the crushed tablets on her fingers.

findings.claim: Nothing in the text gives Cassandra access to Derek's pill bottle — the only documented theft of that bottle belongs to Marcus — so the crushed tablets she uses appear in her hands with no producing act.
findings.citation: Cassandra crushed several of Derek's prescription benzodiazepine tablets — she had observed his pill habit closely in her role monitoring company health — dissolved them in Derek's tumbler

findings.claim: The rinsing of the tumbler is asserted as a fact but no character performs it — the solution has Cassandra leave and re-lock the door, and no one else is placed with the tumbler before discovery.
findings.citation: The tumbler had been rinsed — the inside is damp — suggesting someone attempted to dilute or obscure the residue after the fatal dose was administered.

findings.claim: E3 is tagged red_herring, but the act that produced it is not innocent: Marcus stole the victim's pills, photographed the label and researched lethal doses under a folder name announcing intent — a genuinely culpable act left dangling with no resolution.
findings.citation: Marcus had stolen Derek's prescription pill bottle from his desk drawer two weeks earlier, photographed the label, and researched the lethal dose range.

findings.claim: Step 4 clears Marcus and Priya on the grounds that they lacked closet access, but the murder method is dosing a portable drinking vessel, which requires no closet access at all — the elimination reasoning is invalid.
findings.citation: he researched dosage but had no access to the locked closet and his rooftop discrepancy only shortens his alibi without placing him inside; Priya's idle server session is suspicious but explained by her reading the fax and agonizing over confronting Derek, and she had no closet access

findings.claim: Jin's own alibi has him hearing voices he attributes to Derek on the phone two minutes after he watched Cassandra walk into that same closet, which is internally incoherent and weakens the E6 testimony that Step 2 rests on.
findings.citation: He heard raised voices from inside the server closet around 10:50 PM but assumed it was Derek arguing on the phone as usual.

findings.claim: The idle-session timings do not match: Priya's alibi starts the 47-minute gap at 10:44 PM, while E5 starts it at 10:31 PM and ends it at 11:18 PM, so players cannot reconcile the one document that supposedly breaks her story.
findings.citation: Priya Osman's developer credentials opened a code repository session at 10:31 PM but registered no keystrokes or commands for the following 47 minutes until 11:18 PM

findings.claim: Marcus's rooftop duration is stated two incompatible ways — roughly 105 minutes in his alibi versus 45 minutes in E8 — so the "discrepancy" the clue is built on cannot be measured.
findings.citation: The rooftop deck ashtray contains exactly one cigarette butt, despite Marcus Tull claiming to have smoked three to four cigarettes during his claimed 45-minute stay on the roof.

findings.claim: The cigarette pack exists in two contradictory states and places — half-smoked on the rooftop in the alibi, and near-full in his jacket in E8 — so the physical clue has no single producing act.
findings.citation: A full pack with only one cigarette missing was found in his jacket pocket.

findings.claim: Chemical identification of a benzodiazepine compound, fingerprint isolation on a fax, and residue matching all occur inside a building that is sealed until dawn with four laypeople and no investigator or lab, so no act in the scenario produces this forensic knowledge.
findings.citation: identified on close inspection as the same benzodiazepine compound found in Derek's tumbler

findings.claim: The setting says four people are locked in, but five are present before the murder (Derek, Priya, Marcus, Cassandra, Jin), leaving the victim outside the scenario's own headcount.
findings.citation: meaning all four people present cannot leave until the facilities manager arrives at dawn

findings.claim: Cassandra's motive is thin for premeditated murder: her spying was sanctioned by a powerful investor who could vouch for her, the threatening CEO was himself about to be exposed for a secret IP sale and falsified pipeline at a company with two weeks left, and the only financial upside is explicitly called modest.
findings.citation: She also stood to receive a modest severance bonus triggered only upon the CEO's departure under the company's wind-down policy.
